title: Add drift-detection and canary-prober orchestration to VPC observability TF module
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a set of Terraform resources and orchestration primitives in the VPC observability module to detect infrastructure drift, run canary prober jobs for Prometheus/Grafana/OTel upgrades, and surface failures before a global rollout. The module should: 1) Deploy optional lightweight prober workloads (K8s Jobs or Fargate tasks) that exercise the entire observability path: scrape -> ingest (OTLP) -> storage -> query -> alerting; 2) Provide a drift-detection Lambda (or scheduler) that runs a terraform plan against the module state and reports unexpected changes to Slack and the Console; 3) Add upgrade hooks that gate version rollouts (collector/prometheus/operator/grafana) behind prober success and configurable time windows; 4) Standardize log-shipping config (S3/HTTP) and ship sample logs during canaries to validate parsing and retention; 5) Expose probe metrics and SLOs in the Console for fast rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module adds optional 'prober' boolean flag; when true, prober resources are created and annotated
A scheduled drift-check runs daily (configurable) and creates a Console incident and Slack alert when plan shows changes not in allowed list
Canary upgrade flow: new collector/prometheus image deploys to 2% of nodes, prober jobs validate end-to-end, and rollback triggers if >1 prober failure in 30 minutes
Logging canary: module can provision a sized S3 bucket + IAM role and run a sample log shipper to validate parsing rules and retention lifecycle
implementation_steps: Design: define prober test matrix (scrape, OTLP ingestion with short TTL, dashboard query, alert fire/resolve) and allowed failure thresholds
TF module: add 'prober' submodule supporting both k8s_job and ecs_task execution modes with images and RBAC variables
Drift detection: implement a lightweight lambda that runs 'terraform plan -detailed-exitcode' against the module state bucket and writes findings to a Dynamo table for Console UI
Upgrade hooks: add 'pre_upgrade_probes' and 'post_upgrade_probes' hooks in module API; wire to canary rollout orchestration in the control plane
Log shipping: create example FluentBit/Vector config templates with S3/HTTP outputs and a templated test payload generator
Testing: add unit TF tests (terratest) and integration harness in staging cluster; create GH workflow to run canary simulations
Docs: author console playbook for interpreting prober metrics and executing manual rollbacks or forced-green steps

notes: Trade-offs: running a full terraform plan daily increases API calls and can surface noisy diffs from transient resources (e.g., autoscaler). We'll implement an allowlist of resource types to ignore and a 'drift_tolerance' window.
We chose prober jobs that exercise the OTLP path instead of synthetic metric injection to better validate collector config and mapping transformations.
To avoid extra cost in small accounts, prober default is off. Recommended enabling for Dedicated and Private customers with SLA requirements.
Collector upgrades: include both RPM/container patch paths. Provide rollback image tags and integrate with existing rollout policies in the control plane.
risks: Drift lambda requires elevated read access to remote state and workspace; misconfiguration could leak resource ids—apply strict KMS and VPC endpoints
Probers may add load to small clusters leading to noisy alerts—provide throttling and resource requests/limits
Automatic rollback on false-positive probe failures could impact ongoing maintenance windows—we need a manual override and a quiet-window configuration
qa_plan: Create a staging workspace that mirrors customer VPC settings and run full canary pipeline end-to-end
Simulate drift by mutating a remote state resource and verify drift-lambda reports expected diff and creates a Console incident
Run controlled collector and Prometheus image rollouts in staging with intentional config regressions to validate probe detection and rollback behavior
Verify log shipping canary writes to S3 and that lifecycle policies remove test objects within configured retention
observability_tests: Probe metrics: prober_success_ratio (should be 100% during baseline), probe_latency_ms (p95 < 500ms for query step)
Drift alerts: slack notice and incident ticket created for plan exit code 2 with diff summary
Upgrade SLO: canary group must meet 3 consecutive successful probe runs within a 20 minute window before promoting
Log shipping verification: sample log ingestion time < 60s and parsing errors < 1%
